newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen opening higher.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen opening higher.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open higher Thursday, boosted by a report of strengthening personal computer sales to corporations and a possible settlement in the tobacco talks.

"We're probably headed for a higher opening after three days of a slight pullback," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "The bull continues to show strength with little sign of giving up any time soon."
Larry Wachtel, an analyst at Prudential Securities, said technology stocks could be helped by a Wall Street Journal report that corporate demand for personal computers was strong.

Major computer resellers to corporations indicated there was a slump in demand for PCs that spilled into April from the first quarter, according to the report. But the slump was over by May and demand has been strong in June, it said.
Markets also could be boosted by reports of progress in the talks between state attorneys general and tobacco industry executives, analysts said.
"The Dow will be helped by (component) Philip Morris" if a settlement is announced, Wachtel said.
Japan's Nikkei average closed up 10 points at 20,507.85, boosted by buying by arbitrage traders.
In London the FTSE 100 was down 20.6 points at 4636.4. U.S. stocks were mixed in London, with attention focused on Philip Morris, up 3/4 at 46-1/4.
The dollar stayed in a tight range against the yen, trading at 113.40/50 yen in Tokyo. In Europe the dollar stood at 1.7302/12 marks.
The 30-year U.S. Treasury bond was off 2/32 to yield 6.69 percent. The Standard and Poors 500 futures index was up 1.20 at 900.40.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that rainy, cool weather is starting to hurt the earnings of more and more companies as consumers cut back or delay warm-weather purchases.
The New York Times said in its Market Place column that the move to a single European currency could inspire central banks to sell off even more of their gold.
